   MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  July 10, 2025

Chairperson Victor H. Juan called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m.
Commission members present were Anthony Armendarez, Alejandra Hernandez, Victor
H. Juan, David King, Briana Martinez, Antoinette Moreno, Monique Yanez, and Don
Valenzuela. Commissioner Francisco Berberabe was absent.

Staff Present included Director of Recreation and Park Services Allan Perdomo,
Recreation Superintendent Sonia Batres, Recreation Coordinator Vicki Gonzalez,
Recreation Coordinator Patricia Santana, Recreation Leader III Ariana Ortega, and
Office Assistant II Vanessa Piceno.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Martinez motioned to accept the May 8, 2025, meeting minutes.
Commissioner Armendarez seconded the motion. All in favor.

Commissioner Martinez motioned to accept the June 12, 2025, meeting minutes.
Commissioner Yanez seconded the motion. All in favor.

REPORTS

New Staff Introductions

Director Allan Perdomo introduced newly hired staff member, Recreation Leader III
Ariana Ortega.

Independence Day Festival Re-Cap

Recreation Coordinator Patricia Santana gave a re-cap presentation on the
Independence Day Festival, which took place on Thursday, July 3, from 4:00 p.m. to
9:30 p.m. at the new location, Holifield Park. The event featured live music, a dance
area, a fun zone, 13 food trucks, and a fireworks show, with an estimated attendance of
over 5,000 people. Shuttle services that were provided to and from the event, with
pickup and drop-off locations at the Civic Center and Waite Middle School, helping to
ease parking challenges. Additional parking was available on Norwalk Blvd and
Excelsior Drive, as both streets were closed to allow for expanded event parking.
Recreation Coordinator Patricia Santana and Director Allan Perdomo addressed all
questions and comments from the commissioners following the presentation.

Parks and Recreation Month
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
July 10, 2025

Recreation Coordinator Vicki Gonzalez gave a presentation on July 2025 Parks and
Recreation Month, highlighting the National Recreation and Park Association’s (NRPA)
selected theme, “Build Together, Play Together.” She shared that the Recreation team
developed a calendar featuring daily events and activities throughout the month to
celebrate. The month officially kicked off with a celebration at the Norwalk Arts and
Sports Complex, which featured a festive parklet setup including coffee, pan dulce,
chips, lemonade, iced tea, games, and more. Vicki also announced the upcoming Bark
and Brew event, scheduled for Saturday, July 12, at Robert White Park from 9 a.m. to
12 p.m. She invited Commissioners to attend and help spread the word. Attendees will
be able to enjoy coffee and the dog park, and access dog licensing services onsite.
There were no comments or questions following the presentation.

Norwalk Park Expansion Project

Director Allan Perdomo provided a presentation on the Norwalk Park Expansion Project.
David Volz Design was awarded the contract through the Request for Proposals (RFP)
process to plan and design the Master Plan for Norwalk Park. To support grant funding
efforts, a series of community engagement meetings are being conducted to provide
information on the development of the Master Plan. Funding is being provided through
the Technical Assistance Program (TAP) under the Regional Park and Open Space
District (RPOSD). Two community engagement meetings have already taken place on
June 25 and June 28, and a final meeting is scheduled for July 17, during which the
final concept will be presented for public feedback. Following the presentation, Director
Perdomo addressed all questions and comments from the commissioners.
Fiscal Year 25-26 Department Budget Overview

Director Allan Perdomo provided an overview of the Department Budget for Fiscal Year
2025-2026. On June 6, 2023, the City Council adopted the 2023-2025 Strategic Plan,
which requires each department to align its budget with the plan’s four main goals. For
this fiscal year, capital expenditures include increasing hours for Recreation Leaders II
and III, making general improvements to recreation facilities, replacing aquatic pool
tarps and lanes, enhancing the lobby, gym, and reservation areas at the Norwalk Arts
and Sports Complex, redesigning the Holifield Parking Lot, and completing several
carryover projects from the previous fiscal year. The FY 2025-2026 Budget is available
for public viewing on the city’s website.
Park Projects Monthly Update

Director Allan Perdomo provided updates on current and upcoming park projects. He
began with an overview of the Syserco Energy Solutions project, reporting that the work
at Gerdes Park Field 1 has been completed. The next phases will include Ramona Park
and Lakeside Park, with dates yet to be finalized. The installation of HVAC units at the
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
July 10, 2025

Cultural Arts Center has been completed. Installation at the Norwalk Arts and Sports
Complex is tentatively scheduled for August 18. Solar panel array installation, at the
Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex, is expected to begin on July 21 and continue through
November 28. The installation at the Aquatic Pavilion is scheduled to take place from
August 11 through December 10. For Hermosillo Park, Director Perdomo shared that
the Final Park Concept has been reviewed. Due to budget constraints, the splash pad,
basketball court, and handball court have been removed from the current plans and
replaced with an open natural grass area. The department will continue to evaluate the
feasibility of installing these amenities in the future as funding becomes available. At
Robert White Park, the camera and Wi-Fi installation remains pending until the park’s
master plan is completed. In addition, welded signage has been successfully installed at
both Norwalk Park and Ramona Park. Director Perdomo addressed all questions and
comments from the commissioners following the presentation. There were no further
questions.

STAFF COMMENTS

The first Summer Concert on July 9, featuring Grupo Neblina, was a success at the new
location, Norwalk Park. Join us for the Bark and Brew event at Robert White Park on
July 12, in collaboration with the Finance Department to promote their new dog
registration software. A barista will also be present to serve delicious coffee. Event
details and the parking map can be found on social media. The second Norwalk Park
Planning and Design Community Engagement meeting will take place on July 17. The
first Front Street Concert will take place on July 18 and will feature New Romantics, a
Taylor Swift tribute band.

COMMISISONER’S COMMENTS

Commissioner Moreno – No comment.

Commissioner Yanez – Shared that the Vista Verde Park splash pad is greatly
appreciated by her children and the community. She also gave a shout-out to the
Recreation staff.

Commissioner Armendarez – Expressed enjoyment of the Independence Day Festival
and suggested adding a shuttle pick-up and drop-off site at Social Services. He also
attended the Summer Concert, noted the strong attendance, and appreciated the
presence of the Teen Alliance Program (T.A.P.) volunteers. He looks forward to the
upcoming Norwalk Park Community Engagement Meetings.
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
July 10, 2025

Commissioner Valenzuela – Expressed disappointment that basketball and handball
courts were not included in the Hermosillo Park conceptual designs.

Commissioner King – Commissioner King stepped out before the Commissioner
Comments and did not provide a comment.

Commissioner Martinez – Was pleased with how well the Independence Day Festival
event turned out. She also attended the Norwalk Park Community Engagement meeting
and noted appreciated the collaboration between the team and community members.

Commissioner Hernandez – Attended the Summer Concert and complimented the
event layout. Though she was unable to attend the Independence Day Festival, she
was glad to hear that it was successful. She reminded fellow Commissioners of the
importance of their roles and voices, especially regarding feedback like the Hermosillo
Park conceptual designs. She emphasized their ability to make recommendations and
bridge gaps between the city and the community.

Chairperson Juan – Agreed with Commissioner Valenzuela’s comment about the
absence of basketball and handball courts in the Hermosillo Park conceptual designs.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
Brian Tindall
Jack Cornejo
NEXT MEETING
August 14, 2025

There being no further business to discuss, Chairperson Juan motioned to adjourn the
meeting. Seconded by Commissioner Martinez. All in favor. The meeting was adjourned
at 7:30 p.m.
